prompt: From 'P ∨ Q' and 'P', can you validly conclude '¬Q'?
options: No, because 'or' allows both P and Q to be true
Yes, because only one side can hold
Yes, since P is already true
hint: In logic ∨ is inclusive: 'P or Q' allows both to be true.
explanation: No. ∨ is inclusive, so P ∨ Q allows both to be true, and knowing P says nothing about Q. Disjunctive syllogism needs ¬P to conclude Q.
